definitions.gloss: to squeeze out; to wring out
definitions.explanation: To physically twist or squeeze something to extract its contents.

definitions.gloss: to come up with; to devise with effort
definitions.explanation: To produce an idea, answer, or solution through great mental effort, as if wringing it out of one's brain. Implies difficulty and strain.

examples.japanese: チューブから{最後|さいご}の{一滴|いってき}を{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I squeezed out the last drop from the tube.

examples.japanese: {雑巾|ぞうきん}を{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}すように{水|みず}を{切|き}った。
examples.english: I wrung the rag to squeeze out the water.

examples.japanese: {残|のこ}りわずかな{歯磨|はみが}き{粉|こ}を{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}して{使|つか}った。
examples.english: I squeezed out the last bit of toothpaste and used it.

examples.japanese: やっとアイデアを{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I finally came up with an idea.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}り{間際|まぎわ}に{知恵|ちえ}を{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I racked my brains and came up with a solution right before the deadline.

examples.japanese: {苦|くる}しい{言|い}い{訳|わけ}を{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}して{場|ば}をしのいだ。
examples.english: I came up with a strained excuse and managed to get through the situation.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 2 (figurative) is more common in everyday speech. The word vividly conveys the effort and strain involved in producing something, as if physically twisting it out. Often used with {知恵|ちえ} (wisdom), アイデア (idea), {答|こた}え (answer), and {言|い}い{訳|わけ} (excuse).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {知恵|ちえ}を{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}す (to rack one's brains)
- アイデアを{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}す (to come up with an idea)
- {言|い}い{訳|わけ}を{捻|ひね}り{出|だ}す (to come up with an excuse)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}す: to squeeze out — very similar, but more emphasis on squeezing than twisting
- {思|おも}いつく: to think of — neutral; lacks the connotation of effort and struggle
